title: Winter Light Cathedral
location: Aotea Square, 291-297 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Wander through a glowing tunnel of light and feel the magic of winter come alive!
Step inside Winter Light Cathedral - a dazzling, walk-through experience made from tens of thousands of tiny LED lights. Inspired by the sweeping arches of grand church windows, this luminous tunnel invites you in for a moment of warmth, wonder and a little bit of WOW.
From the outside, it shines like a beacon in Aotea Square. Inside, it’s something else entirely - a sparkling, cosy world where every step surrounds you in soft, golden light.
Subtle by day and radiant after dark, whether you're out for a family night or date night this is a joyful experience not to miss.
Walk it once, snap a pic, tag us @aucklandlive, then go again - you’ll want to!
Hot tip: Visit on a Friday or Saturday night, between 6pm and 9pm, to watch neon-lit dancers bringing an extra touch of magic to the Cathedral. 
Free entry, just turn up and step into the magic. Open 24/7 (best to visit after dark).

title: 3 Volcanoes (Mt Eden, Mt St John & Mt Hobson)
location: 250 Mt Eden Road, Mt Eden, Auckland
description:
We will be walking a loop in central Auckland to include 3 volcano summits: Maungawhau / Mount Eden, Te Kōpuke / Mount St John, and Ōhinerau / Mount Hobson. Amazing views over the harbour and city.

Graded 2 on our 1-5 difficulty rating - some steep sections climbing up to the top of each volcano. Otherwise mostly easy on gravel paths or pavement.

Approx: 2 - 2.5hrs of walking (depends on the group)
Distance: 9.5km

**Here's the plan:**

Before 10:30am - Meet at the Tahaki Reserve carpark, 250 Mount Eden Road. If that carpark is full you can find street parking in the surrounding streets.

\*Please note, there are no toilets along our walking route. You can use either the toilet around the corner at the Tahaki Reserve Playground, or the public toilets on Puhi Huia Road inside Mt Eden domain. -36.874886, 174.764401

10:30am - Start walking up and around Mt Eden, then over to Mt St John and Mt Hobson, returning to our starting point via Newmarket.

\*Please note, we will be crossing a couple of busy roads. For safety purposes, where possible, we will cross as a group at traffic lights.

1.00pm - Anticipated finish time

**Bring** \- Normal hiking gear \- the tracks are fairly well\-maintained so you can wear running shoes with good grip instead of hiking boots\. Hat\, rain jacket and warm layers to wear or keep in your pack\, plus drink bottle\.

**Food** \- Bring your own snacks and water\.

**Carpooling** \- Please comment when you rsvp whether you need a lift / can offer lifts\, which part of Auckland and your mobile number\. It’s up to you to arrange this among yourselves\. Please bring $10 cash for your drivers or make arrangements to pay your driver by bank transfer\. You could also catch public transport \(bus\) to our starting point\.

No guests. If you have friends who would like to come get them to join Auckland Outdoors and RSVP.

If your situation changes and you can no longer attend please update your RSVP immediately. If you drop out after 5pm the night

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
location: 96 Saint Georges Bay Road, Auckland
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please use the following link to pre-register for Xero Venue before arriving** [https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/O8Ih4IdzCowjvyIM](https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/O8Ih4IdzCowjvyIM).
* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: From Zero Interviews to Real Projects: What to Build When No One's Calling Back? by Ismael Silva**
This talk is aimed squarely at where most of the room actually is right now — applying, waiting, wondering if the market has forgotten about them. The core idea is that waiting is the worst use of a junior's time, and there's a better way to spend those weeks that turns a CV into a portfolio and an interview into a conversation about something you've actually built.

The session will show that "building leverage" does not require massive side projects. It will also touch on the value of soft skills and leadership, making the discussion relevant for both junior and experienced developers.

**A bit about Ismael:**

* Ismael is a full-stack engineer specializing in Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, and Postgres, and currently runs a small product studio called Base Logic Labs. Before transitioning into tech, he spent more than 20 years in public speaking, sales, and leadership roles, delivering over a thousand talks across various settings.

**Talk 2: How Fast Can You Rise? by Katrina Clokie**
Katrina meets a lot of ambitious young people who seem to believe that it's possible for them to advance in their careers at an aggressive pace (once they get their foot in the door). description:
Hello everyone,

We're excited to invite you to the **Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup**!

This month, we are diving deep into the realities of moving AI from a cool demo to a production-ready system. We are thrilled to host two fantastic co-speakers: **[Roger Wang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roger-nz/)** (Senior Solutions Architect @ AWS) and **[Saurabh Gupta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nzsaurabh/)** (Pushpay).

We are gathering once again at the *Pushpay office in the CBD*—looking forward to seeing you all there!

**🎤 The Lineup**
**Roger Wang (AWS) & Saurabh Gupta (Pushpay)**

* **Title:** Breaking Through the 65% Ceiling: How Pushpay Engineered a 95% Accurate Production AI Agent
* **Description:** Agentic AI plateaus fast once you move beyond demos. Pushpay's natural language search agent hit a \~65% accuracy ceiling before the team built a structured evaluation framework to break through it.
Roger and Saurabh will walk through Pushpay's real-world journey: building the agent on **Amazon Bedrock**, why accuracy stalled, and the engineering techniques that pushed it to 95%. They will share practical takeaways including constructing a 300+ query golden dataset, automating measurement with LLM-as-a-Judge, and applying domain-specific prompt engineering on Bedrock. No hype—just real numbers, a real production system, and actionable insights for anyone building or operating agents.

title: Tāmaki after dark
location: Whare Wānanga, Level 2, Central City Library, 44 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
For over a hundred years, the heart of our city hasn’t just beaten - it’s pulsed to a rhythm.
Join us for a high-energy journey through time, tracing the evolution of the music scene from the stiff collars of formal dance halls to the sweat-soaked rock gigs and smoky underground cabarets of the 1960s, then on to the modern world of nightclubs and music bars.
We’ll explore how shifting laws and cultural revolutions shaped the sounds of the city, and how the music, in turn, changed us forever.
Gareth Shute writes regularly for the NZ music history website Audioculture | Iwi Waiata and is also the author of six books, including the recent work: Songs From The Shaky Isles: A Short History of Popular Music In New Zealand. He is also a musician, who has played everywhere from the scummiest dive bars on K Rd through to the stage of the iconic Powerstation.
Tāmaki untold: conversations celebrating the taonga, stories and creativity of Auckland. A curated monthly talk series held in the Whare Wānanga hosted by Research and Heritage Services, Auckland Libraries.
